column4: dialect-gated per SUBTEST: a registeredBackends test, so it runs one subtest per dialect and mysql and mssql skip in these PostgreSQL-only jobs while postgres RUNS -- two, not three. Measured by name rather than by delta, with CLEAT_TEST_MYSQL and CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL unset. Guards cleat#1153: a pre-emptive cancel records 'cancelled' as a terminal status AND still runs the defers it owes, which is the constraint the repository owner attached to the feature. The arms have to exist even where they skip, because the two-phase transition is written separately per dialect -- engine/db.go, engine/mysql_ops.go and engine/mssql_operations.go each hold their own preemptivelySettle, with different placeholder syntax and different now() spellings -- so a postgres-only run cannot vouch for the other two. Falsification confirms it: recording 'terminated' instead of 'cancelled' fails the MARK arm, and routing unconditionally through MARK fails the one-step arm, independently per dialect.

dialect-gated per SUBTEST: same test, same two arms, and the cluster job runs ./engine/... too, so these two lines move together -- scripts/skip-ledger.d/README.md says so. Same measurement and same reason as the test-go/engine line above; see cleat#1153.
